The Battle of Kisangani took place in August 1999 during the Second Congo War between Uganda People's Defense Force in conjunction with RCD-Kisangani, and the Rwandan Patriotic Front alongside RCD-Goma, over strategy and tactics concerning the overthrow of Congolese President, Laurent Kabila.
With Wambia having just defected from the greater Rally for Congolese Democracy, in the lead up to the battle, claims were disseminated among the RCD-Kisangani that up to 4000 RCD-Goma troops were approaching from Goma to recapture the previously Rwandan-held city. Fighting ultimately erupted on August 14 at the Kisangani Bangoka International Airport, with both sides contending the other was the one that issued the first shots. Both sides utilized heavy weaponry and carried out the battle in the streets of residential areas, continuing until the ceasefire on August 17th. The conflict was ultimately ended when the greater RCD agreed to sign the Lusaka Ceasefire Agreement.
